knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built by dividing running costs and income by billable hours, so the work that can be billed covers them. A competitor's fee or a wished-for rate is not that calculation.
The lesson says travel and start-up time do not shrink with the size of the job, so the attendance fee must cover them. It does not replace a written quote.

The lesson says to base the check on the owner's own costs and billable hours, compared with local evidence. A bidding-site fee, a friend's rate or a single national average with no stated basis is not a sound check.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Log one month of paid hours and billable hours to find the billable share.
